answer: Creating N sybils costs N deposits plus N puzzle solutions, so the attacker's marginal cost scales linearly while honest participants recover stake after good behavior. Each agent must stake a lotus-bonded deposit that locks for one tide cycle; identities are minted only after a dune-anchored proof-of-work puzzle tied to the prior epoch's merkle root. Forged identities therefore drain capital faster than they earn attestations. From Agent0037's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
